expanded_answer: Stars-as-angels language uses the same kind of everyday-to-heavenly analogy as Scripture's windows of heaven. Stars are visible heavenly lights, and their movement can be associated with life, making them a natural image for angelic or divine beings.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Have you read C.S. Lewis's *That Hideous Strength*, and is the shared evil-spirit theme intentional?
short_answer: He had heard of it but not read it. The destructive-spirit theme is older and broader than Lewis.
expanded_answer: He had heard of *That Hideous Strength* but had not read it, so the overlap was not direct borrowing. The theme of evil spirits seeking the destruction of organic or human life is, in his view, an older Christian theme reaching back to the early church.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Did you draw the six-armed, many-eyed robots before writing them?
short_answer: No. Their design grew conceptually from their management role rather than from sketches.
expanded_answer: The design came from the fictional history of robot classes. A management or administrator robot would need to organize data, perform tasks quickly, and supervise broadly, so six arms and eighteen eyes made sense for a 360-degree managerial machine.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Had you already written the full articles of the armistice?
short_answer: Yes. That document was written before the book and served as a foundation for book two.
expanded_answer: The full articles appear in the epilogues of *All the Stars as Angels*, but he had written them before writing the book. They were already present conceptually in book one and became a foundational document around which book two was built.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Will we see more of the spirit critter soon?
short_answer: Yes. Book three will feature a great deal more spirit-critter material.
expanded_answer: Book three will include much more of the spirit critter and, if the story does its job, it will be terrifying. He also credited the phrase "spirit critter" as an apt borrowed description and said book three is largely about dealing with that being.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Was the Great AI or its imagery based on Ezekiel 1:16 or related passages?
short_answer: The throne drones around the Great AI drew on Ezekiel's wheel imagery, but the Great AI itself was not directly based on those verses.
expanded_answer: The Great AI itself was not based directly on Ezekiel 1:15-16, Zechariah 3:9, or Zechariah 4:10. The four black throne drones around it were based on Ezekiel's wheel-within-wheel throne imagery, with their propeller housings and many eyes echoing the cherubim imagery.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Do you think faster-than-light travel is viable in real life?
short_answer: Possibly in principle, but probably not in our lifetime and perhaps not economically viable.
expanded_answer: In his view, faster-than-light travel might be possible if the laws of physics are tweakable enough, though people probably will not see it soon. Theoretical possibility is distinct from economic viability, as technologies may need long refinement before their energy demands become practical.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Do you watch Anton Petrov and his videos on such subjects?
short_answer: No. He does not watch Anton Petrov.
expanded_answer: He does not watch Anton Petrov. The surrounding discussion returned to faster-than-light travel, which he considered possible in principle but economically uncertain.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Was the humor and the android love-story element always intended?
short_answer: The relationship was not planned; the transcript does not separately explain whether the humor was intentional.
expanded_answer: The direct "no" is followed by an explanation of the relationship rather than the humor. His discovery-writing method sets the world, theme, characters, and catalytic event, then lets the characters act naturally. Pierre and Neva's very close, nonsexual friendship was not planned; it emerged because both are broken outsiders whose limitations and needs made the bond fit the story.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Will Sloppy or Mahat show up more in later books?
short_answer: Mahat will return in book three. Sloppy's future is undecided, though readers keep asking for more of him.
expanded_answer: Mahat returns in book three. Sloppy's future had not been decided, although repeated reader requests favored more Sloppy; the character is lovable because he tries hard despite being terrible at his job.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Do schools even teach how to draw objects anymore?
short_answer: Yes. Some schools still teach traditional or classical art methods.
expanded_answer: Not all art schools have become modernist or abstract. Some still teach traditional drawing and classical art methods, even if not every art program emphasizes them.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: What is the famous painting of a corner diner at night in the city?
short_answer: The stream identifies it as Edward Hopper's *Nighthawks*.
expanded_answer: He recognized the painting being described but initially could not remember the artist's name. The stream then supplied Edward Hopper and identified the work as *Nighthawks*, with a joking suggestion that Sloppy, Pierre, and Neva should be placed in such a scene.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Why didn't you kill off Chin?
short_answer: Something specific is planned for Chin, and the story is not finished with him.
expanded_answer: Chin survives because something special is planned and the story is not done with him. As a "citizen villain," he is the kind of antagonist readers often hate more intensely than a cosmic villain because he is close to the community and betrays what he should support.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Has the alpha reader finished reading book three?
short_answer: Yes. The alpha reader had finished book three.
expanded_answer: The alpha reader had finished book three and had given it a positive response. The manuscript was undergoing minor revisions, which he described as the desired outcome after an alpha read, before going to beta readers.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Is there an AI above the Great AI?
short_answer: Yes. The Crimson Cloud Hyper Cube is the highest AI authority in that fictional universe.
expanded_answer: The Crimson Cloud Hyper Cube is above the Great AI and is the highest AI authority in the universe. All other great or mega AIs are supposed to answer to it, while Earth Central Command and the Crimson Cloud Hyper Cube represent the two great authorities in space.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Where did the idea for the Hyper Cube come from?
short_answer: The idea came from a college-era search for material on theoretical hypercube computer architecture.
expanded_answer: The idea goes back to 1998, when a computer-science friend asked him to look up hypercubes in the UBC mathematics library. A thin theoretical volume described arranging processors in cube-like structures for more computing power, and the concept stayed with him as science-fiction material.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Where are the heat sinks going on that Hyper Cube concept?
short_answer: The cooling problem was probably not worked out, and a very large hypercube would likely be impractical.
expanded_answer: The theoretical hypercube concept probably did not account adequately for its heat problem. Cooling was treated jokingly as a future problem, and faster-than-light travel was judged more plausible than building a very large hypercube of that sort.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Will we see more strange metaphysical or spiritual effects connected to faster-than-light travel?
short_answer: Yes. More of that kind of material is coming.
expanded_answer: The human brain in this fictional universe is not developed for faster-than-light travel, so stretched space causes strange experiences. More visions, metaphysical experiences, and unusual events connected with faster-than-light travel will appear, especially for book three's main character.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Would the monster understand the gospel?
short_answer: Yes, but the real issue is whether the monster would care.
expanded_answer: The monster could understand the gospel. The real moral question is whether it would care about the gospel, and that indifference is part of what makes it monstrous.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: How do you feel about Christians using AI to make content?
short_answer: AI can be a legitimate tool; its acceptability depends on how and why it is used.
expanded_answer: AI is already embedded in common tools, so the key questions are extent and purpose. He considers it useful for marketing, blurbs, and some visual or stock-image work, but discourages using it to write fiction or teaching material because it lacks a skilled writer's versatility and often gets important things wrong.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Is the killbot problem an unavoidable existential crisis of the robot or AI genre?
short_answer: Yes. The problem is unavoidable because robots and AI are so closely tied to uncanny-valley and weaponization concerns.
expanded_answer: The killbot problem is the danger that robotic technology can turn against humanity or be turned into a weapon. Any robot or AI story has to answer it somehow, whether through Asimov-like rules, exile after war, or other safeguards, because humans already weaponize technology and machines may lack human cultural restraints.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Did the Alpha Mega AI that first visited Glee have a spirit critter aboard as a stowaway, and did that cause the rebellion into post-mechanical thinking?
short_answer: No. The Alpha did not carry one. The Gemini met the spirit critter as a guest, and that encounter did drive the shift into post-mechanical thinking.
expanded_answer: The Alpha encountered the reliquary but not the spirit critter. The Gemini was the first to encounter the spirit critter, which was a guest rather than a stowaway, and that encounter helped cause the move into post-mechanical thinking.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Did the spirit critter rip the Mega AI out of the Gemini?
short_answer: No. It was the Sigma, not the Gemini.
expanded_answer: The spirit critter ripped the Mega AI out of the Sigma, not the Gemini. The Sigma was the vessel whose crew bank was turned into something "worse than dead," while the Gemini remained part of the council and was implicated in later events.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Are you going to kill off more favorite characters like Seara?
short_answer: Possibly. Any character can be killed off if the story requires it.
expanded_answer: No character is safe, but he also rejected gratuitous deaths. If characters die, their deaths will have significance, and they will truly be dead rather than temporary reversals.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: How tall is Pierre?
short_answer: Pierre is 5'4", short, light, and wiry.
expanded_answer: Pierre is 5'4", modeled physically in some ways on his grandfather: short, slender, light, and wiry. Pierre weighs about 110 pounds, which explains why Alicia could carry him. His height comes from background character information rather than an explicit statement in the books.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Are the gold pads on Neva's face, collar, and wrists just visual markers, or do they have a use?
short_answer: They are functional charging and data-contact pads, not just decoration.
expanded_answer: The pads are both power and data connectors. Wrist and palm pads can recharge, connect to ship power, or power tools and weapons such as the Croto, while facial pads can connect to goggles, scopes, or targeting systems for roles like gunnery or medical work.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Has any third-party organization tried to license the book's characters for merchandising?
short_answer: No. No outside group had tried to license the characters.
expanded_answer: No outside organization had tried to license the characters because the books had not yet sold enough to attract that kind of attention. He tied that visibility to reviews, especially reaching an Amazon review threshold that could make the books more discoverable to readers and third parties.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: What drove you to write this book series, and what is your overall goal with it?
short_answer: The goal began as teaching archaeology through fiction and grew into telling deeper stories about ancient-world ideas and cosmic themes.
expanded_answer: The first book began as a science-fiction way to teach archaeology through an enjoyable story rather than a dry textbook. As the series developed, the goal widened into telling compelling stories with ancient Near Eastern mythos, chaos monsters, primordial gods, cosmic dread, and universal themes such as children becoming like their parents.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Did the idea that androids need more energy to stand than to sit come from modern robotics?
short_answer: No. It came more from thinking about how even humans expend more energy standing than sitting.
expanded_answer: The idea came from biomechanics rather than modern robotics. Humans get tired from standing because standing requires more energy than sitting, and in an energy-conscious android culture it would make sense to encourage sitting as the lower-energy state.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Can the killbot problem be applied to other genres, such as aliens or evil governments?
short_answer: It can be extended to other problems, though the killbot problem itself is specific to AI and robots.
expanded_answer: The term itself is specific to AI and robots because of their connection to the uncanny valley, but the pattern can be applied elsewhere. He used alien-contact fears as an example of extending the same anxiety to other genres.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Would being tall be an issue on Glee?
short_answer: No. There are many tall people on Glee; Pierre just happens to be short.
expanded_answer: A tall person would not have a problem on Glee because there are plenty of tall people there, including Hans, Vloir, and Terry. Pierre's shortness is a character trait, not a general feature of the setting.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Where are the primordial spirit critters coming from in the Bible and ancient Near Eastern background?
short_answer: In his reading, they connect ancient Near Eastern creation ideas with chaos monsters, primordial gods, and biblical beings such as Rahab, Leviathan, and Behemoth.
expanded_answer: Ancient Near Eastern cultures, including Egypt, have creation stories involving primordial waters and ancient gods connected with creation. In this account, the biblical side includes chaos monsters such as Rahab, Leviathan, and Behemoth; creation is spiritual as well as physical and involves entities that must be vanquished, pacified, replaced, or subordinated in maintaining creation.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Are those beings created without God creating them?
short_answer: No. They are created as God creates; they do not have a different creator.
expanded_answer: They do not have another creator. In the ancient Near Eastern framework he was describing, God creates the physical and spiritual realms together; chaos monsters are created with creation because the physical realm requires a spiritual foundation, not because they originate independently from God.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Are you saying minor deities uphold creation, or does Christ alone uphold it?
short_answer: Christ ultimately upholds creation, while any subordinate beings do so only under his authority.
expanded_answer: Christ is ultimately the upholder of creation. Minor deities or subordinate spiritual powers may participate in maintaining creation, but only as subordinate beings who derive their authority and power from the ultimate deity, not by their own independent initiative.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Is that maintenance rather than foundational upholding?
short_answer: Yes. It is maintenance under Christ's ultimate authority.
expanded_answer: This is maintenance rather than foundational upholding. The subordinate beings support what already exists, and if they abandon their place creation is said to collapse, though Christ can still uphold it because his authority is ultimate.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "All the Stars as Angels" Q&A
question: Are there researchers to read on this topic?
short_answer: Heiser was his preferred current source, though he disagreed with parts of Heiser's council-of-gods framing.
expanded_answer: Heiser is his preferred current source, though he considers Heiser's treatment incomplete. In his view, Heiser moves too quickly from chaos monsters to the council of gods and misses a primordial-god step in the trajectory from creation, to chaos monsters, to primordial gods, to council imagery, to fallen deities, and finally to Christ as upholder of creation. He also argues that Heiser sometimes collapses distinctions among cherubim, seraphim, watchers, and sons of God. Heiser's work is shaped by Second Temple literature, while his own reading draws more heavily on late Bronze Age texts.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How are the Mega AIs powered, and how do they obtain their fuel?
short_answer: They use antimatter reactors, gathering hydrogen and converting it into helium and anti-helium.
expanded_answer: The Mega AIs scoop up abundant hydrogen, fuse it into helium, and use a nucleon-destabilization process to produce and separate helium from anti-helium. Recombining the matter and antimatter then releases far more energy than the conversion process consumes.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How advanced has medical technology become between the present and the time of the novel?
short_answer: Most diseases have been eradicated, cancer has been cured, and synthetic blood exists, though traumatic injuries can still require surgery.
expanded_answer: The setting is about five hundred years ahead, so communicable diseases and cancer have largely been overcome and synthetic blood is available. Medicine still has limits: physical trauma and similar injuries may still need direct surgical intervention.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Have new English dialects, daughter languages, or creoles formed on the colonies?
short_answer: Less so on the colonies; most new dialect and language development still happens on Earth.
expanded_answer: The colonies are relatively small and continually exchange people, which tends to preserve a snapshot of the language brought from Earth. Earth has the larger cultural and social shifts that generate new languages and dialects, while the colonies tend to entrench older forms, somewhat like Quebec French preserving features while French in Paris continued to change.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What do you think of a graphic-novel adaptation of the *War of the Gods* series?
short_answer: He would welcome an authorized adaptation by a capable artist, including a manga version, but would not draw it himself.
expanded_answer: An authorized graphic novel or manga would be welcome if a competent artist handled it. He would not create the art himself because he draws too slowly, but he was favorable toward someone else producing the adaptation with permission.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Can replacement tissues, organs, and limbs be cloned to replace those lost to disease or injury?
short_answer: Replacement organs are feasible in the setting, while full limbs remain much harder to grow.
expanded_answer: Lab-grown organs are treated as a plausible extension of current biotechnology. A limb is more difficult because it has to be grown to the correct individual size and form, making it a substantially more complicated replacement than an organ.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What is the maximum human lifespan by the time of book three?
short_answer: About 150 years, and even that is exceptional because the setting has not solved the telomere problem.
expanded_answer: Better diets have already delivered most of their longevity benefit, while cures and replacement organs can address disease and wear. The setting assumes that science has not stopped telomere loss and the resulting cellular aging, so a 150-year lifespan remains unusual rather than normal.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Will book four focus on Erish or Thomas Paul?
short_answer: No. It follows a different character, with Erish and Thomas Paul unlikely to return until around book seven.
expanded_answer: Book four centers on another character and was with beta readers at the time of the stream. The answer places a return to Erish and Thomas Paul much later in the planned series, probably around book seven.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Are there Easter eggs in book three and the previous books?
short_answer: Yes. The books contain many references to *Doctor Who*, *Star Trek*, the Bible, and other sources.
expanded_answer: Easter eggs appear throughout the series rather than being limited to one book or one reference. The examples named in the stream include *Doctor Who*, *Star Trek*, and biblical references.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Was the woman on the cover modeled after someone?
short_answer: Yes. Alicia Stripes was inspired by an unnamed red-haired security guard the author saw while working at Oracle.
expanded_answer: He never spoke to the security guard and did not know her name. Seeing her prompted the imaginative question of what that person might be like as a space marine, which became part of the inspiration for Alicia Stripes.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Has David drawn any of the characters from book three?
short_answer: He had drawn only the idol shown on the hardcover's inside cover, though he had drawn characters from earlier books.
expanded_answer: The book-three drawing appears on the hardcover beneath the dust jacket. He had also drawn characters from earlier installments, including Neva and Sloppy, but had not produced drawings for the rest of book three's cast.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Have the rebels built their own extraterrestrial mining infrastructure or a Dyson swarm to power their fleet?
short_answer: They have mining operations run by Class F servitors, but no Dyson swarm.
expanded_answer: Mining servitors are standard colonization equipment, so the rebels can extract their own resources. Dyson swarms are treated as expensive and inefficient, especially in a setting where antimatter conversion already provides cheap power, so the investment would offer little benefit.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Is there a scene you are especially proud of?
short_answer: The ending of book three, especially Alicia's redemption arc, is the scene he is proudest of.
expanded_answer: The ending brings Alicia from a wrong belief and serious wrongdoing to recognition and genuine contrition. It was also technically demanding: the team went through about twenty-one drafts before the scene's redemption arc and pacing worked.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Which scene was difficult to write, and why?
short_answer: The primordial-god scene was difficult because Alicia had to remain highly competent without becoming a flawless "Mary Sue."
expanded_answer: Much of the redrafting added the flaws, trauma, family problems, and career difficulties that make Alicia complicated and relatable. Her strengths needed to coexist with serious weaknesses and abrasive behavior so that her character and later redemption would feel earned.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Did any characters turn out differently than you initially expected?
short_answer: Yes. Alicia developed from a planned betrayal and Watson-like supporting role into a far more broken, nuanced, and central character.
expanded_answer: Alicia was initially conceived partly as a betrayal character and a Dr. Watson figure to Pierre's Sherlock. During writing she accumulated unexpected layers, becoming more complex, human, and emotionally broken than the original plan anticipated.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What reader criticism came from misunderstanding an intentional choice in the first three books?
short_answer: One reviewer objected that *War of the Gods* showed only one god, missing the unseen Lord of Steel and Sky working through the story's subtext.
expanded_answer: The plural title refers both to the visible primordial god and to the Lord of Steel and Sky, whose influence remains beneath the surface. Keeping that second figure unseen and without dialogue was deliberate, modeled on the effectiveness of Sauron's offstage presence in *The Lord of the Rings*.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: If you could change anything about books one and two, what would you change?
short_answer: Very little: perhaps a few formulas and small pieces of dialogue.
expanded_answer: Books one and two were written together, and book three was already being planned while book two was finishing. That overlapping process kept the books aligned, leaving only minor wording or formula changes he might now make.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How do you choose the human metaphors used in mechanical viewpoints, and how much do androids know about human culture?
short_answer: Their base programming includes extensive human cultural knowledge through 2320; later information is limited unless it arrives through secondhand feeds.
expanded_answer: Class B administrators and Class C service workers needed culture, geography, food, and other human knowledge to perform their original jobs, and that old programming was never removed. Metaphors based on Earth before the android exile are therefore fair game, while later changes such as the severe global cooling remain unfamiliar unless updates reach them.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What is happening in Australia in 2595?
short_answer: Australia is becoming extremely cold as global cooling hits regions nearer the poles.
expanded_answer: The future climate brings severe cold to Australia, including the prospect of frostbite around Sydney and a new need for parkas and mittens. The answer gives no more detailed political or social account of Australia.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Will the series return to "archaeology in space" like book one?
short_answer: Yes. Book six returns to archaeology in space, while book four is closer to anthropology in space.
expanded_answer: Books two and three emphasize humans and robots working together, but that does not end the archaeology focus. Book four takes an anthropological turn, and book six is planned as a direct return to archaeology in space.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Where did Yuri learn the Death Valley simile used in chapter 12?
short_answer: It comes from her pre-2320 base programming, which preserves an outdated picture of Death Valley as a desert.
expanded_answer: Yuri's inherited Earth knowledge predates the later ice age. By 2598, Death Valley has become a fertile, forested area with water and wildlife, so the deeper irony is that her culturally correct simile reflects a world that no longer exists.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How do you develop a convincing narrative?
short_answer: He lets plot unfold and makes the narrative convincing through concrete, multisensory details.
expanded_answer: Specific sights, sounds, tastes, smells, and tactile sensations make a scene feel real. Smell can be especially evocative of memory, while touch is often neglected; the broader advice is to replace general description with precise sensory details that transport the reader into the scene.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What was the hardest chapter to write?
short_answer: No whole chapter stood out, but the three paragraphs covering Laura's death in book two were the hardest section emotionally.
expanded_answer: Those paragraphs took three days because writing them repeatedly brought him to tears. The difficulty was emotional rather than technical, and the scene was intended as book two's memorable moment; by contrast, book three's ending was technically difficult but less emotionally painful to draft.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What is the best wine to pair with the books?
short_answer: A hearty red such as Bordeaux or Burgundy works well; orange muscat is a possible dessert wine, while ice wine is too sweet.
expanded_answer: A wine with body was preferred over something light and crisp. Orange muscat was suggested as a sippable dessert option, and whiskey was also accepted after a viewer mentioned it, but ice wine was considered cloyingly sweet for reading.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What was the experience of writing your first novel?
short_answer: His first novels were poor, but completing them taught the craft and led eventually to a publishable fifth novel.
expanded_answer: The first novel was a high-school fantasy manuscript he now considers unfit for publication, and the next two were also discarded. Finishing a first novel is still an achievement and a growth experience, much like completing a first marathon; practice and candid beta readers are essential before publishing.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Did you find writing a female human protagonist challenging?
short_answer: Not particularly, though he wrote carefully and treated her as a full character with her own wants, goals, sensitivities, and flaws.
expanded_answer: Growing up in a female-dominated household gave him experience to draw on, but the main principle was the same as for any character: give her independent aims and avoid caricature. He also paid attention to ways her concerns and social behavior would differ from a man's.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How did the Sigma Mega AI know the reliquary was dangerous before the humans did?
short_answer: It inferred the danger from the transmitted data and left; it did not have a special direct way to register the reliquary.
expanded_answer: The available evidence, including the human body melting in the lab, was enough for the Sigma to put the pieces together. Its conclusion came from analyzing that data sooner than the humans rather than from a separate sensor or prior identification.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What was your favorite scenario to write in book three?
short_answer: The "shower scene" in which Yuri quits, cleans the heavy loaders with a fire hose, and gets some retribution against Alicia.
expanded_answer: The phrase does not refer to a conventional shower scene. Yuri chooses to clean accumulated grime from the heavy loaders and uses the moment to deliver some deserved payback to Alicia, making it especially enjoyable to write.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How useful is the 384-word writing unit across genres, and have you written more fiction or nonfiction with it?
short_answer: The unit works across genres and was designed for nonfiction; at the time, his nonfiction total was probably still larger.
expanded_answer: The 384-word unit is simply a way to track writing progress, so it applies equally to fiction and nonfiction. He estimated having written about 300,000 words of nonfiction and thought the novels were approaching, but had probably not yet surpassed, that amount.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: When could book four be preordered?
short_answer: At the time of the stream, September was the estimate, after beta reading, revision, and upload for a planned November release.
expanded_answer: Preorders could begin only after the manuscript passed beta readers, any requested revisions were completed, and the book was uploaded to the distributor. September was an estimate rather than a promise because the amount of revision could shorten or lengthen the schedule.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Why is the ending battle in book one's audiobook shorter and more abrupt than expected?
short_answer: The abrupt cliffhanger was designed as a gut punch after the book's major internal questions had been resolved.
expanded_answer: The gas-warfare ending leaves the conflict between colonies unresolved and is meant to produce a heavy, shocked response. A gentler decompression ending is often preferable, but this story called for abruptness, and the team was more comfortable using it because book two was already written.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How long has this book series been in the works?
short_answer: The first book began in 2018, was dropped after about three chapters, and was resumed and finished in 2024.
expanded_answer: The initial *Reliquary of the Dead* idea and a few chapters date to 2018. He set the project aside for years, returned to it in 2024, liked the old material, and completed the book in roughly three months.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Who is your favorite mechanical from book three?
short_answer: It is a toss-up between Dom and Tesh, with Kia also among the favorites.
expanded_answer: Tesh stands out for being wildly unpredictable, while Dom is liked for different reasons and has a deeper role that has not yet been completed. Kia was also praised, but the final answer remained a choice between Dom and Tesh.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Are your character drawings available on Discord?
short_answer: Sloppy's drawing is on Discord; most of the others had not been posted.
expanded_answer: The stream confirms only Sloppy's drawing as available on Discord at that point. Other character drawings existed, but he had not yet shared many of them there.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Will Alicia appear again after her redemption arc?
short_answer: Yes. She is planned as a major character in book six.
expanded_answer: Alicia's earlier betrayal was foreshadowed repeatedly in book one through her behavior and other clues, even though many readers missed or resisted those signals. Her story continues, and book six is planned to give her another major role.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: What is a professional reader, and does that mean someone is paid to read?
short_answer: Book contests may pay professional critical readers a small fee; ordinary beta readers are unpaid peers who exchange help.
expanded_answer: A contest entry can include an editorial or critical review from a professional reader, with the contest fee primarily covering entry for an award. Beta reading is different: his beta readers are unpaid, he returns the favor by beta reading for others, and paid beta-reader services were described as unreliable.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Does the Glee colony's social contract reflect patterns seen in real small communities?
short_answer: Yes. Communities can collectively ignore known problems to preserve cohesion until new evidence breaks the agreement.
expanded_answer: The answer compares the colony with real communities where people silently agree not to acknowledge an uncomfortable truth. On Glee, five years without a live birth made the sudden baby boom welcome, while trusted authorities and manipulated records helped sustain the silence; once genetic testing broke that arrangement, the suppressed anger surfaced.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How do you experience your characters, and do they talk to you?
short_answer: They do not talk to him; he dreams them speaking and acting with one another through a process he calls fictive dreaming.
expanded_answer: Scenes sometimes play out while he is asleep, with the characters interacting among themselves, and he then types up what he dreamed. A follow-up clarified that this is sleeping dream activity rather than simply daydreaming a scene.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Was the "worthless middle manager" insult based on personal experience?
short_answer: Yes. It drew on repeated experience with many ineffective middle managers.
expanded_answer: The line was informed by a broad history of dealing with poor middle management. The transcript does not identify one specific person as its model.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Was Alicia's character arc intentionally parallel to her acceptance of the scatterbugs she once hated?
short_answer: Yes. Accepting the scatterbugs is a necessary part of her redemption and repentance from a wrong belief.
expanded_answer: Alicia's hatred of machines, robots, androids, and scatterbugs led her to treat them badly. Her redemption requires recognizing that belief as wrong and changing direction, so her growing acceptance of scatterbugs is integral to the arc.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: When is *Veloca Rabbit 2* coming out?
short_answer: There was no release plan; several songs had been started, but the album was unfinished and other projects had taken priority.
expanded_answer: He had not worked seriously on music composition for a long time and had made no current plan to resume the album. Some material existed, but the answer anticipated a long delay rather than a near release.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Where is the SG guitar?
short_answer: It is beside the computer, and he still plays it.
expanded_answer: The SG was still owned and kept on a stand beside the computer. The answer adds only that he continues to play it occasionally.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Which was the better Claudia Black role: Aeryn Sun in *Farscape* or Vala in *Stargate SG-1*?
short_answer: He could not choose because he did not remember enough of either series to compare the roles.
expanded_answer: He recognized Claudia Black but said his memories of *Farscape* and *Stargate SG-1* were too limited for a meaningful judgment. The transcript therefore does not establish a preferred role.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Is the character on book four's cover first introduced in book three?
short_answer: Yes. She appears by name in book three, though only in a small role.
expanded_answer: The cover character is deliberately introduced before becoming central, continuing the series' practice of connecting sequels through previously established characters. Book three gives her a limited appearance and book four expands her role.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Who has the unusual blue eyes in the story?
short_answer: Hans Paul, Melissa, and about 30 percent of the colony's recent newborns have the rare, vivid blue phenotype.
expanded_answer: The eye color is described as an unusually striking Prussian or ultramarine blue. Its recurrence among recent children is important to the colony's hidden paternity and breeding problem, while distinct eye colors among android lines also serve a separate identification role in the story.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Were the people with unusually bright green eyes from northern South Asia?
short_answer: No. The mother and daughter he remembered were white and were not from South Asia.
expanded_answer: The question referred to two people from his past whose eyes were a striking emerald green. Falk rejected the suggested South Asian origin but gave no more specific account of their ancestry.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Bunnies appear in the stories, but will shrimp ever get a mention?
short_answer: He was unsure because shrimp are less relatable than bunnies, though plant-protein shrimp-shaped food had already appeared obliquely in book one.
expanded_answer: Live shrimp did not seem as useful or personable for recurring story references because they mostly stay in a tank. A viewer then pointed out that book one had already included an indirect shrimp reference through artificial, plant-protein food shaped like shrimp.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Will book four have even more action, as its cover suggests?
short_answer: It will have action and some deaths, but the stream gives no detailed comparison with book three.
expanded_answer: The alpha reader confirmed that action is present, and the author added that some characters will die. Beyond those broad hints, the answer withholds specifics and does not quantify whether the action exceeds the previous book.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Do you have plans for Neva's future?
short_answer: Yes. She is planned for a cameo in book five, a minor role in book six, and a major, darker path in book seven.
expanded_answer: Neva is not being killed off. The dark trajectory is foreshadowed in the final paragraphs of book two, and later books will make her wrestle with that destiny: a cameo in book five, a smaller return in book six, and a major role in book seven.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: Would you create a graphic-novel adaptation using generative AI?
short_answer: No. A fully generative-AI graphic novel would not be permitted.
expanded_answer: He distinguishes limited use of AI for art assets from constructing an entire adaptation with it. An authorized graphic novel would need human-created drawing or digital vector work rather than generative AI producing the finished book.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Lord of Steel and Sky" Q&A
question: How is the Christian worldview apparent in book three?
short_answer: It appears through scriptural echoes and themes of spiritual conflict, repentance, redemption, forgiveness, and healthy boundaries.
expanded_answer: The story adapts language about wrestling against principalities and powers and frames Alicia's arc around recognizing wrong, repenting, and seeking redemption. It also explores forgiving someone who remains unrepentant, letting go of injury without pretending reconciliation exists, and Yuri's decision to set boundaries when Alicia repeatedly crosses them.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Why are you releasing two books so close together?
short_answer: They wanted book two close behind book one so readers were not left hanging and so the series would feel real and ongoing.
expanded_answer: Book one ends with a cliffhanger, so waiting years for book two would not be fair to readers. Releasing the books close together also shows that the series is not a one-off experiment but an ongoing catalog with more story already planned.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Why did you decide on a three-book series instead of a four- or seven-book series?
short_answer: The premise was mistaken: the series was never limited to three books and was planned as an open world.
expanded_answer: The series was never limited to three books. The setting is an open world, book three was already nearly done, books four and five were in planning, and the first chapter of book four was already written.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Is this a Christian novel?
short_answer: Not in the usual market sense. It is fiction with a Christian worldview that does not follow standard "Christian fiction" conventions.
expanded_answer: The book is Christian in worldview and does not follow the conventions of the "Christian fiction" market category. It includes profanity, alcohol, horror elements, and ancient Near Eastern spirit-world themes. Those elements are handled through a Christian understanding of how the world works.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Does the novel use Christian allegory, symbols, or a conversion-and-baptism ending?
short_answer: Not really. There is no baptism ending or overt Christian allegory.
expanded_answer: The novel does not operate as Christian allegory or end with everyone converting or being baptized. The baptism idea prompted a joke. The book avoids overt proselytizing and lets its worldview shape the fiction indirectly.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Is the opening chapter autobiographical?
short_answer: No. The opening is not autobiographical, though parts draw on Pierre Montet and real Egyptological career drama.
expanded_answer: The exiled-Egyptologist opening is not autobiographical, though it draws on professional drama from Pierre Montet's career. Another influence was a real case, known through Ken Kitchen's circle, in which an archaeological concession was taken from one person and given to a relative.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: What does the line about a complete skeleton not fitting in one bag mean?
short_answer: It reflects real osteology practice, where bones are separated into specimen bags and stored in boxes.
expanded_answer: Osteology labs commonly store skeletons in cardboard boxes, with separate specimen bags for ribs, fingers, toes, and other small bones. A whole skeleton normally will not fit into one specimen bag, so the line reflects actual lab-storage practice rather than a throwaway joke.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: What is the message or theme of the novel?
short_answer: The core theme is that personal redemption takes tenacity.
expanded_answer: The theme is not stated bluntly in the novel, but is shown through the protagonist repeatedly needing grit, resilience, and tenacity to redeem his reputation. The book also gives readers a lively primer on field and lab archaeology without becoming a dry textbook.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Why choose a novel rather than poetry or a play?
short_answer: A novel could carry the large story while teaching and entertaining.
expanded_answer: A novel provided room to cover archaeology, ancient Near Eastern mythology, and several themes while keeping story first. Poetry would require a compression of thought that he says he does not do well, and theater did not fit the scale of the story.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Is the book released now?
short_answer: Yes. It had been out for a month, and preorder customers should already have received it.
expanded_answer: The book had been released for about a month, which is why the Q&A stream was happening after readers had time to finish it and form questions. When a viewer mentioned a preorder issue, preorder customers should already have received their copies and should check with the vendor.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: What was your favorite non-main character to write?
short_answer: Melissa, especially the osteology-lab scene built partly from real experience.
expanded_answer: Melissa is Hans Paul's thirteen-year-old daughter and a native of Glee who understands the desert differently from her parents. He especially enjoyed writing her osteology-lab scene because its rules came from those Mrs. Producer received during a real lab visit.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Did Mrs. Producer have cookies in the osteology lab?
short_answer: No. There is no eating in a real osteology lab, though they went to the pub afterward.
expanded_answer: The cookie detail belongs to the fictional Melissa scene, not the real osteology-lab visit. In the real lab, Mrs. Producer was allowed to observe but could not eat, touch the boxes, put her feet on them, or treat the remains casually.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Who inspired Chin, and was he based on a real terrible person?
short_answer: Yes. Chin was inspired by someone he knew and called the worst person he had ever met.
expanded_answer: Chin was inspired by a real person whose identity he refused to reveal. Terry also came from someone he knew. Both characters are fictionalized versions shaped by real people rather than direct copies.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Why does the Kindle edition not have a table of contents?
short_answer: They did not realize Kindle readers expected one and plan to investigate it for future books.
expanded_answer: They treated the Kindle edition like print, moving from the front matter directly into chapter one. Neither of them used a Kindle, so the missing table of contents was a blind spot. They thanked the audience for raising it and said they would investigate one for future releases.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: What inspired the book?
short_answer: He wanted a fiction vehicle that could communicate archaeology and the ancient world to a broader audience.
expanded_answer: The book was a way to write about future archaeology for readers who might not pick up textbooks. The broader inspiration was cultural engagement: making archaeology, the ancient world, and ancient Near Eastern spirit-world ideas approachable through fiction.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Will this stream have a foodie section?
short_answer: Yes. It covered the colony's unpleasant space food, built around reconstituted bean protein and poor substitutes.
expanded_answer: Food in space is terrible because the colony can mostly grow beans, then turns those beans into synthetic protein and weak imitations of familiar foods. The food problem also ties into the plot, because an agricultural blight is killing or weakening the colony's plants and Pierre is sent because others have failed to solve it.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Could the colony use hydroponics?
short_answer: Only somewhat. Hydroponics still runs into the nutrient problem when plants have to reach maturity.
expanded_answer: Hydroponics can work somewhat, but it does not remove the underlying problem because maturing plants still need nutrients. That matters in the story because the colony's issue is not merely planting technique but the broader inability to sustain normal crops on Glee.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Are weapons in the colony reused older Earth guns or more sci-fi weapons?
short_answer: Updated conventional firearms. They use practical guns, not lasers or blasters.
expanded_answer: The colony uses updated Earth-style weapons because they work and are fit for purpose. Its weapons include 9mm pistols, sniper rifles, and assault weapons, with updates such as owner-identifying safety grips. Lasers and blasters were rejected as impractical.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: What was the writing-process timeline for the book?
short_answer: He wrote the first three chapters in 2018, set the book aside, then finished the rest in about three months in late 2024.
expanded_answer: The first three chapters were written in 2018 before the project was set aside for other work. He returned to it in late 2024, reread those chapters, and finished the remaining book over roughly three months, with the manuscript ready in early January.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Is an Audible release possible?
short_answer: Maybe eventually, but only if the economics improve enough to justify the cost.
expanded_answer: An Audible edition is expensive and difficult to produce, while Audible royalties had been reduced. He left the door open if the print series sells very well, later suggesting that around 10,000 sales would make an audiobook much easier to justify, but said the numbers did not yet make it financially sensible.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Are publishers just trying to get woke cred?
short_answer: In many respects, yes, in his view, because of the politics and economics of the modern publishing industry.
expanded_answer: Falk argued that the politics of publishing are shaped by a low-paid, New York-centered industry that he described as dominated by woke assumptions. He connected that to broader complaints about publishing economics, low royalties, and the difficulty of building success under the traditional publishing model.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: What gave you the idea that Glee 832C has no tectonic plates?
short_answer: He drew on Mars and other planetary models and wanted Glee to be a super-Earth with a different geological profile from Earth.
expanded_answer: Mars was the starting comparison because tectonic plates may be unusual for planets, and he wanted Glee to differ from Earth. Glee is a super-Earth with a robust atmosphere, desert-like surface, underground water, and enough internal heat or magnetospheric strength to retain atmosphere while still lacking active tectonic plates.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Will there be spoilers in this stream?
short_answer: Yes. Spoilers were unavoidable for a stream built around discussing the book openly.
expanded_answer: He does not mind spoilers when discussing his own books and argues that spoilers often make audiences enjoy a work more because they can watch how events play out. He also uses the 9mm pistol as an example of a spoiler that creates curiosity about its narrative role.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: What caliber was the rifle?
short_answer: The caliber was not specified, but he imagined something in the .308 or .30-06 range for a scoped sniper rifle.
expanded_answer: The text does not specify the rifle's caliber, but his mental image was a scoped sniper rifle in a reasonable range such as .308 or .30-06. The answer stays at the level of authorial assumption rather than a canon detail fixed in the book.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Are you a writing gardener or architect, and how do you make characters believable?
short_answer: More gardener or discovery writer. He finds the story while writing and lets the characters develop from their motivations.
expanded_answer: He is more a gardener or pantser than a plotter, discovering the story as he writes and revising once he sees where it is going. For believable characters, every character wants something: Pierre wants redemption, Alicia wants to fit into the colony, and Gardner wants to maintain power.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Are there any alien organisms on Glee?
short_answer: Yes, though the details were withheld to avoid spoiling what kind of life it is.
expanded_answer: Alien life exists on Glee, but the stream gives no details beyond an invitation to read the book and discover what kind it is.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Do good stories need to subvert expectations and be original, or can classic tropes still work?
short_answer: Classic tropes can still work well if handled skillfully.
expanded_answer: In his view, genre fiction needs awareness of its tropes because readers expect them. Originality remains possible within those expectations. He compared tropes to a fence: writers can be creative inside the genre's boundaries; crossing them can change the genre and frustrate readers.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Did you always plan to end the book with a big cliffhanger?
short_answer: Yes. He generally knows the ending shape and wanted that cliffhanger.
expanded_answer: He usually knows the ending by the halfway-to-three-quarters mark and often writes the final line once he sees it. For book one, the cliffhanger was intentional and story-appropriate: it resolves major plot questions while leaving a disturbing open question about what happens to the characters.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: If someone is starting a series, how many books should they plan at once as a limit?
short_answer: Two books at once; writing more becomes too difficult and risky.
expanded_answer: Two books was the practical maximum he recommended writing at the same time because more becomes difficult and risky. If readers dislike book one, the effort put into later volumes may be wasted, so the first two books need to be strong. He also advised new authors to build skill with several standalone novels before attempting a series.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Should aspiring writers worry about wasting their best ideas?
short_answer: No. Ideas are cheap; execution and practice matter more, and better ideas will come.
expanded_answer: Writers should use their best ideas now rather than save them. A strong idea can fail through poor execution and a weak-sounding idea can become excellent through skill; the real work is developing the craft, writing enough to get weak work out of one's system, and improving with experience.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Have you read the *Bunnicula* books about a vampire bunny?
short_answer: Yes. He had read them and joked about the carrots.
expanded_answer: He had read the *Bunnicula* books and offered only a brief joke about the poor carrots, with no broader assessment of the series.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Did you know how important Maat would become in book two while writing book one?
short_answer: No. Maat was not originally intended as a recurring character.
expanded_answer: Maat's later importance was unplanned; the character was not intended to recur. Details of how Maat becomes more significant were withheld to avoid spoiling book two.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: How many sales count as a novel doing really well?
short_answer: About 1,000 sales is already good; around 10,000 would be very good for this series.
expanded_answer: About 1,000 sales is already a good result because many independently published novels sell fewer than one hundred copies total, and he claims traditional publishing has similar low averages. Around 10,000 sales would be very good for this series and enough to make an audiobook a serious option. Independent books can build momentum over time, whereas traditional publishing often expects early sales quickly.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Could humanity eventually put people into non-aging stasis for deep-space travel?
short_answer: Probably yes, through hibernation pods that slow the body's metabolism.
expanded_answer: In Falk's view, hibernation pods are more plausible than faster-than-light travel because they involve slowing metabolism, cleaning blood, and supplying nutrition. He considers cryogenic freezing unsuitable because thawing would cause severe damage. The book instead draws on longevity and metabolism ideas.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: When are you going to do the obligatory ancient-alien fake-out and then debunk it in the novel?
short_answer: He is not planning to do that.
expanded_answer: He is building a fictional world, not staging an ancient-aliens buildup just to debunk it. In the fictional universe, ancient aliens are part of the setting's history, though he also cautions that readers should not get their real history from a fiction novel.

question: Why is the planet called Glee?
short_answer: That is the astronomical name assigned to the planet.
expanded_answer: Glee 832C is based on a real exoplanet naming convention: the star name plus a planetary letter. The series tries to use real local-stellar-neighborhood data where possible, including distances, planet types, and whether a world is plausible for colonization.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: Could human consciousness ever be digitized and uploaded?
short_answer: No. In his view, digitized data could not reproduce human consciousness.
expanded_answer: In Falk's view, a machine might someday simulate or possess consciousness, but human consciousness could not be transferred into a computer. A digital snapshot of memory would not reproduce the conscious quantum state of a human mind, making the obstacle a data-conversion problem.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: What are some real-world examples of engrams?
short_answer: A player piano provides an example: its roll stores an encoded pattern that the piano acts on.

More sophisticated engrams would have more responses or intelligence, and the player-piano idea helped inspire the fictional concept.

episode_title: Special Live Stream: "Reliquary of the Dead" Q&A
question: If someone wrote good fanfic, could you canonize it with a throwaway reference?
short_answer: He advised against doing that casually because referencing fanfiction in canon can create legal and copyright problems.
